title: Camp Evergreen

subtitle.text: It was the first day of summer camp.
Ivy was not happy as she rode in her family's van.
She drew a picture in her sketch pad, trying to imagine Camp Evergreen.
She sketched an ugly building.
Around it was a high electric fence.
A sign on the front said Evergreen Prison.
She drew counselors who looked like zombie guards.
All the campers wore prison outfits.
Ivy was [i@supposed@i] to go to Camp Kahlo, an art camp. But Camp Kahlo was full.
So her parents signed her up for Camp Evergreen instead.
"There's the camp sign!" Dad called from the front seat.
"You'll have such a great time here!" Mom said.
"There are so many fun outdoor activities."
Ivy slid down in the seat. "I hate the outdoors, remember?"
"Don't be silly—you love the outdoors," Mom said.
"Remember our picnic last summer?
You skipped through the meadow, picking wildflowers."
"No, I tripped over a tree root and got stung by a wasp," Ivy said.
"We're here!" Dad said cheerfully as the van pulled into a parking lot.
Suddenly the door on Ivy's side of the van opened.
A woman wearing an army cap poked her head inside.
A whistle hung from a string around her neck.
"Greetings, camper! Private Nelson here!" she shouted.
"Yikes!" Ivy thought, climbing out of the van.
"She looks just like the zombie guards in my drawing!"
All around them, kids and parents carried suitcases, duffels, and sleeping bags.
Dad tried to shake hands with Private, but she saluted him instead.
"This is Ivy's first summer at camp, so she's very excited!" Mom said.
Ivy rolled her eyes.
Private crossed her arms and looked Ivy up and down.
"I'm in charge of all sports. Soccer, baseball, tennis, swimming, canoeing.
What's your favorite sport?"
"Drawing," Ivy said. "I also like painting."
"Hmm, we do have arts and crafts twice a week," Private said.
"And when it rains. If you like that kind of thing."
Ivy's parents unloaded her stuff.
Private blew her whistle.
The shrill noise made everyone jump.
A young woman wearing a Camp Evergreen T-shirt came running.
"Hi, Ivy! I'm Penelope, one of the camp counselors!
I'll bring you to your cabin."
Ivy's parents hugged her good-bye.
"Send lots of letters!" Dad said.
"Have a great summer, sweetheart!" Mom said.
"Yeah, right." Ivy moaned.
"This place is worse than prison."
She gave her parents a sad wave as the van drove away.
"Camp Evergreen is the absolute best summer camp in the world!"
Penelope gushed as she and Ivy walked across the parking lot.
"I've been coming here since I was six. I'm full of Evergreen spirit!"
"Evergreen spirit?" Ivy thought. "What the heck is that?"
Penelope showed her a large building called the lodge.
"The mess hall and kitchen are in here. The food is sooo yummy!"
"It smells like . . . dirty socks," Ivy muttered.
Next Penelope pointed out the activity rooms and the square, a wide, grassy outdoor area.
"That path leads to the sports area.
There are tennis courts and soccer and baseball fields.
The girls' cabins are this way," Penelope said.
"But first I'll show you the showers."
They approached an old, rundown building.
Penelope showed Ivy the showers.
Ivy peered into the dark, damp stalls.
The paint was peeling, and the floors looked green and slimy.
"There's somebody in this shower," Ivy said with a shudder.
"Somebody with eight creepy legs!"
"Don't worry, Ivy!" Penelope said.
"That spider is only a daddy longlegs."
She brushed the spider off the shower wall.
"Just a part of beautiful nature!"
"I think nature is . . . unnatural," Ivy said.
Penelope laughed. "You're funny, Ivy!"
They continued toward the girls' cabins.
At Cabin 6, Penelope threw open the screen door. "Here's our cabin!"
Inside were bunk beds and shelves for personal items.
Two girls were sitting on one bed, giggling together.
"Ivy, say hi to your bunkmates—Clara and Willow," Penelope said.
"That's my bunk. You can have this one."
Ivy put her suitcase down. "Hello."
"You girls make Ivy feel at home.
When the bugle sounds, come to the square for some Evergreen spirit!" Penelope said.
"Why does she keep talking about Evergreen spirit?" Ivy thought.
After the counselor left, the two girls looked at Ivy.
"So . . . what kind of music do you like?" Clara asked.
"Yeah, do you like K-pop?" Willow asked. "Those singers are the cutest!"
Ivy sat on her bunk. It sagged in the middle.
The springs made a loud squeak.
"My favorite band is Graveyard Puppies."
She opened her suitcase and pulled out the band's poster.
Clara and Willow stared at the creepy image.
Then Clara laughed nervously. "We'll have to check them out."
A second later a bugle sounded.
Willow looked relieved. "Time for the welcome games!"
"See you at the square," Clara said.
Ivy sighed and grabbed her sketch pad and colored pencils.
She trudged behind the other campers walking to the square.
Penelope stood in front with a male counselor.
"Hello, campers! Let's play a get-acquainted game.
Larry will explain the rules."
Larry wore sunglasses and had long hair.
"Yeah, so, you're going to say your name.
And then say some animal that starts with the same initial.
Like, hey, my name is Larry, and I love lizards."
Ivy moved to the back of the group.
"Like, this is the lamest," she whispered, opening her sketch pad.
Clara picked a cheetah for her animal, and Willow chose a whale.
Then Larry called on a boy named Ezra.
"I know him from school," Ivy thought.
Ezra froze for a second. "Uh, m-my name is Ezra," he said.
"And I love . . . er, elephants!"
For the next few minutes, Ivy was busy drawing.
Suddenly she noticed how quiet it was.
She looked up to see everyone staring at her.
"Your turn!" Penelope called.
Ivy sighed and flipped through her sketches.
"My name is Ivy, and I love ivy—poison ivy."
She held up a drawing of the plant with three leaves.
"Ew!" a few kids said.
Ezra started scratching himself.
"I got a rash from poison ivy last summer!"
Willow frowned. "Poison ivy isn't an animal."
Ivy shrugged. "I'm an independent thinker."
Wes Wheezer, the bugle boy, blew his instrument again.
It was time for dinner.
As everyone headed to the mess hall, Ezra walked beside Ivy.
Clara and Willow walked with them too.
"Can I see more of your art?" Ezra asked.
"You seem to have a lot of talent," Clara said politely.
Ivy flipped through the pages.
"I was working on this self-portrait."
She showed them her latest sketch.
It was a drawing of Ivy looking terrified.
Her mouth was wide open.
In the background was Camp Evergreen with a scary, orange-and-yellow sky.
"I call it 'The Scream,'" Ivy said proudly.
"Because that's what this camp makes me feel like doing!"
Willow frowned at Ivy's sketch.
"Camp Evergreen is awesome. All the kids here love it."
"Well, [i@most@i] of the kids," Clara said.
"Why don't you show some Evergreen spirit, Ivy?"
Ivy sighed as the girls hurried away.
Then she walked with Ezra into the mess hall.
They picked up trays and got in line.
"What's this Evergreen spirit stuff?" Ivy asked.
"It's being happy and excited about camp." Ezra shrugged.
"It's my third year, and I'm still not happy or excited."
"I'll be excited when I leave," Ivy said.
They got some food and brought it to a table.
A boy sat there alone.
"Glen, this is Ivy," Ezra said.
Glen grinned. "Hi, Ivy.
If you want to know anything about Camp Evergreen, just ask me.
It's my second summer. I'm basically an expert."
Ivy stared at the food on her tray.
"My first question is—what's this brown stuff?"
"I think it's hamburger," Glen said.
Ezra sniffed his fork. "Or it might be tofu."
Ivy frowned at the boys. "What about this other brown stuff?"
"Oh, that's potato salad!" Glen said.
Ezra held up his fruit punch. "This drink is called bug juice."
"Because it's made from squashed bugs!"
Glen laughed so hard, bug juice came out of his nose.
Ivy pushed her tray away. "I lost my appetite," she said.
Soon Wes Wheezer blew his bugle.
The kids carried their trays and put them in pans for washing.
Then they left for the assembly hall, another room inside the lodge.
As soon as all the kids and counselors were inside, the lights went out.
The room was pitch black.
"Hey, what's going on?" Ivy asked.
The bugle sounded again.
Then a voice yelled through a loud bullhorn. "Ever!"
"Green!" everyone shouted back.
Bullhorn: "Never!"
Campers: "Not!"
Bullhorn: "How much camp spirit have you got?"
The lights came on again.
Ivy stared at the strange sight around her.
Most of the kids and counselors were singing a song about Camp Evergreen.
They were also doing a crazy dance.
A few kids like Ivy sat on the floor, watching in confusion.
Ezra was sweating as he tried to do the dance.
Glen was the loudest singer, but his awful voice made Ivy cover her ears.
"Now that's some terrific Camp Evergreen spirit!" Penelope shouted.
"Indeed," Private said.
"In fact, we're having a contest in a few days.
It's to see who has the most Evergreen spirit."
"So, like, get in groups of three," Larry said.
"And your group should decide, like, how to show the most Evergreen spirit."
"Ugh," Ivy groaned. "What a dumb idea for a contest."
She went over to join Ezra and Glen.
The three of them listened to the other kids' ideas for a few minutes.
"How about a skit on Camp Evergreen's history?" Clara suggested to her group.
"We could write a new song," a boy named Richard said.
"We're having an arm-wrestling contest!" a tough boy named Buck yelled.
"Winners have Evergreen spirit. Losers are a bunch of wimps who hate camp!"
His friends, Chuck and Huck, laughed.
They grabbed Buck's arms and pulled on them. All three fell over in a heap.
"Ivy, those wrestlers are the Ucks," Glen said.
She wrinkled her nose. "Yuck!"
Ezra looked nervous. "What should we do for the contest?"
"I know!" Ivy whispered.
Ezra looked surprised. "You do?"
Ivy nodded. "Let's break out of this prison camp the first chance we get!"
The assembly was over.
The campers walked across the square in the dark.
Ivy, Glen, and Ezra were still talking about Ivy's idea to leave camp.
Glen used his flashlight to light up the way.
"I don't want to leave.
This is the summer when everyone figures out how cool I am. Finally!"
Ezra bit his lip. "I don't want to get in trouble.
But I wouldn't mind leaving—I miss my parents.
I've already written them two letters."
"Well, I'm breaking out of here no matter what!" Ivy said.
"If you want to come along, we can make plans tomorrow."
The next morning the campers gathered in the lodge after breakfast.
Private was checking each group's plans for the spirit contest.
She walked over to Ivy's group. "State your idea, campers!"
The kids looked at each other nervously.
"We have a great idea," Glen said.
"But we don't want the others stealing it!"
Private jotted a note on her clipboard.
"Got it—top secret," she said before walking away.
Ivy grinned. "By the time the spirit contest happens, we'll be out of here!"
Later that morning a counselor named Mango introduced himself.
He was leading the campers on a nature walk.
Mango peered through a pair of binoculars.
"Today we'll be searching for the blue-footed warbler.
It makes its nests in pine trees." He grinned.
"It's also been known to nest in the soup pots in the mess hall.
Follow me, everyone!"
The kids walked along the hiking trail.
"So," Ivy whispered. "How can we escape?
There's a high fence around the whole camp."
Ezra pulled some rolled-up toilet paper from his pocket.
"My dad is good at building things.
Sometimes I help him. Maybe we can build a catapult."
Ezra unrolled the paper to show them his diagram.
"We can cut down a small tree for the frame.
Then we'll tie the boards together with old strands of spaghetti.
I hear that's what we're having for lunch today."
Ivy made a face. "Is the spaghetti that tough?"
Both boys nodded.
Ivy and Glen studied Ezra's drawing.
"Looks good but where's the bucket?" Glen asked.
"You know—the part we sit in that will launch us over the fence."
Ezra shrugged and looked at his feet.
"I didn't get that far. I ran out of toilet paper."
"Hey, kids!" Mango shouted.
"A rare four-toed salamander!"
Everyone gathered around to look.
"Salamanders are nearly extinct in these woods," Mango said.
Chuck pointed under a log. "There's one."
Huck held up a glass jar. "I caught three yesterday."
"So exciting to see the salamanders making a comeback!" Mango sighed happily.
The group continued their hike.
"I've decided I'll escape with you," Glen whispered.
"Years from now, campers will gather around the campfire.
They'll tell stories about amazing Glen Brown's daring escape.
I'll be a Camp Evergreen legend!"
"Okay, amazing Glen," Ivy said.
"Got any amazing ideas about how to break out of here?"
Glen nodded. "We're surrounded by wild animals.
Why don't we use their techniques? We can tunnel out!"
"Let's stop here for a second!" Mango said suddenly.
Ivy watched Mango crawl through a hole in the fence.
He laid some carrots on the ground.
"For my little opossum friends," Mango said, looking up into the trees with his binoculars.
Ivy turned back to the boys. "Here's an idea.
Why don't we just climb through that hole in the fence?"
Ezra's eyes went wide as he stared at the hole in the fence.
"You want us to crawl through [i@that@i] hole, Ivy?
But what if the opossums attack us?"
Glen laughed. "Opossums are the friendliest forest creatures there are.
Well, unless you wake them up."
Ivy peeked through the hole.
"Guys, this is perfect! We can escape tonight.
Let's meet an hour after the last bugle call."
So that was the plan.
Ivy could hardly wait.
That night she lay in her bunk, listening to all the sounds.
Willow and Clara had finally stopped talking.
Penelope snored softly.
When it was time, Ivy slipped out of bed.
She slowly opened the screen door.
It squeaked a little but not enough to wake up the others.
Ivy sneaked through the dark night toward the square.
Up ahead, she saw what looked like two shining eyes.
"Psst! Glen? Ezra? Is that you?"
"Ivy! Over here!" Glen said a little too loudly.
The two shining eyes were coming from Ezra's face.
"What are you wearing?" Ivy asked.
"These are my homemade night vision goggles," Ezra said.
"I glued two mini flashlights to my glasses."
"Wow, that's pretty cool," Ivy said.
"I mean, if they actually work."
The kids started down the dark trail.
Ezra crashed into Glen, almost knocking him down.
"Hey, watch it!" Glen yelled.
"Sorry," Ezra said.
A few minutes later, Ezra stepped on Ivy's toes.
"Ouch! Ezra, try not to be so clumsy," Ivy said.
"Sorry! I glued the flashlights in front of my eyes.
I can't see anything!"
Ivy sighed. "Try pushing the glasses up on your forehead."
They tiptoed through the woods behind boys' cabins.
They could hear someone strumming a ukulele.
"That's Mango," Glen whispered.
"He thinks ukulele music puts us to sleep."
"That horrible noise would give me nightmares," Ivy said.
Just then Ezra tripped over a rock and made a loud noise.
"Who—who's there?" Mango cried.
Ivy and the boys froze in place.
"Hoo, hoo, hoo, hoo, hoo!" Glen called, imitating an owl.
They heard Mango chuckle.
He went back to playing his ukulele.
Overhead the moon was shining.
Its silver light reflected off the lake.
A million stars winked like tiny lights.
"I hope we don't step on a snake."
Ezra moved his head around so the flashlights lit up the path.
"Snakes like [i@sunlight@i], Ezra," Glen said.
"At night we're more likely to run into skunks. Or wolves."
"W-wolves?" Ezra asked, his voice shaking.
Ivy poked Glen in the ribs with her elbow. "You're not being helpful."
They came to a fork in the path.
Ivy turned right, and Glen turned left.
Ezra stumbled off the path and fell into a bush.
"The hole in the fence is this way," Ivy said.
Glen pointed left. "No, it's this way."
"I think Ivy's right.
I mean, correct. We go to the right," Ezra said, picking leaves out of his hair.
Glen sighed. "We can't get lost.
Then the amazing Glen Brown escape legend won't be very . . . um, amazing."
They hiked down the trail until Ivy stopped suddenly.
"Look! There's the hole in the fence."
She ducked down and crawled through the opening.
Glen was right behind her.
Ezra put one foot through the hole.
Just then a shrill whistle pierced the night.
A bright light shone right in the kids' eyes.
"Freeze, campers!" a voice shouted.
"Don't take another step!"
Past the bright light, Ivy saw a dark silhouette.
"Oh, no! It's Private!" she whispered.
She and Glen climbed back through the hole.
Private loomed over them.
Ezra raised his hand. "H-how did you find us?"
"Security cameras." Private pointed up to the trees.
"I'm on constant lookout for deserters."
Private ordered them to go straight to their cabins.
Ivy gulped. They were in big, big trouble.
The next morning they stood in Private's office, waiting to be punished.
Private blew her whistle, making everyone jump.
Then she glared at them.
“I know why your contest idea was top secret.
You planned to escape!
So now you need to do something positive for Camp Evergreen."
“Sending us home might be positive," Ivy thought.
"You'll paint the showers," Private said.
Ivy groaned. "The showers are disgusting!"
"Yep." Private led them to a supply closet.
Inside were a dozen old, dented cans of paint.
"I'll inspect the job before dinner," she said.
Then she left the kids to their work.
Ezra sighed. "Private should have stayed in the army."
"She left because it wasn't tough enough for her!" Glen reminded him.
The kids grabbed some paint cans and brushes.
They headed first to the boys' showers.
Glen opened a can. "These showers are the creepiest place in camp.
I've heard that bats live in one of the stalls!"
"I stay away from the showers," Ezra said.
"The bacteria levels are deadly."
"Wait—it's your third summer.
You've never taken a shower?" Ivy asked in disbelief.
Ezra shrugged. "I swim in the lake once a week."
Glen gazed into the half-empty paint cans.
"We can't paint the showers. There's not enough of one color."
Ezra bit his lip. "We'll never get this job done!"
Ivy looked at all the different paint colors.
Then she looked up at her friends again.
"Actually," she said slowly, "this is perfect!"
The kids got busy painting.
It was a hot day.
They were sweaty and tired when they finished the boys' showers.
Then they moved on to the girls' showers.
Ezra sat on Glen's shoulders to reach the high spots.
Ivy got green paint in her hair, and Glen's hands were pink and purple.
Right before the dinner bugle blew, Private arrived with Larry and Penelope.
"How beautiful!" Penelope cried.
"That's, like, so colorful, like the way my dreams look," Larry said.
Private gave them a quick nod.
The three painters exchanged high-fives.
The dark, dirty showers had been transformed.
Now there were colorful murals of Camp Evergreen's woods and blue lake.
Ivy had also hidden some fun details—like poison ivy and a creepy daddy longlegs.
That evening during assembly, the campers performed their acts for the spirit contest.
Wes tooted his new song and his friends sang along.
The Ucks arm-wrestled each other.
At last Private blew her whistle to announce the winners.
"Who has the best Evergreen spirit? I think we can all agree.
This year's award goes to . . . " Everyone held their breath as Private paused.
"Three talented painters—Ivy, Glen, and Ezra!"
"Huh?" Ivy blinked.
The crowd burst into applause.
The three campers accepted their blue ribbons.
"I knew I'd be a legend!" Glen said.
"My parents will be so proud!" Ezra cried.
"No way." Ivy stared at her ribbon.
"I can't have the best Evergreen spirit. I hate this place!"
But that thought didn't stop a huge smile from spreading across her face.
Ivy squeezed through the crowd on the porch outside the lodge.
Lunch had just ended.
Now all the campers were checking their mailboxes.
"This is the best time of the day," Ivy thought.
In fact, it was the [i@only@i] time of the day that she liked at camp.
She grabbed an envelope from her mailbox.
"It's from my aunt Lydia. She's awesome.
She understands me better than my parents do."
Ezra didn't answer.
He was reading a postcard.
Glen held up a blue slip.
"I got a package from my parents. Let's go get it."
The kids walked to the office.
"I wrote to Aunt Lydia and told her I hate camp," Ivy said.
"I asked her to rescue me. Maybe she's on her way."
Ivy read the letter.
"Oh, great. Aunt Lydia is at a photography workshop!
She's not coming."
She crumpled the letter and tossed it in a trashcan.
"I guess I'm stuck here."
"I don't believe it!" Ezra said.
"Me neither," Ivy said.
"I'm talking about this postcard." Ezra showed it to Glen and Ivy.
"My parents are at the beach!
They went on vacation—without me!"
"That looks like a fancy resort," Glen said.
"They're probably having lots of fun."
"Of course they're having fun," Ezra said. "Without me!"
"Don't worry," Glen said.
"Whatever I got from my parents, I'll share with you."
The friends walked into the office.
Glen gave the slip to Mrs. Matsak, the camp secretary.
She handed Glen a box.
"It's already opened," Ivy said, surprised.
Mrs. Matsak rolled her eyes. "Private checks all the packages.
She wants to make sure nobody is getting anything that breaks the rules."
"Wow, look!" Glen showed them the box.
It was full of homemade brownies, candy, and gum!
"You can have one treat now, but the rest stays here," Mrs. Matsak said.
"No food in the cabins. It attracts ants and wild animals."
Glen sighed. "Okay."
They each took a brownie.
A deliveryman came in, sweating as he pushed a handcart.
On it was a statue of a tall bear carved from wood.
"Where should I put this?"
"Wonderful! It's here," Mrs. Matsak said.
"Put it in that corner. Soon it will be placed in the square."
"Too bad it's not a real bear," Ivy whispered.
"They'd have to close camp and send everyone home!"
Glen glanced at Mrs. Matsak.
She was still talking to the deliveryman.
"Psst! Grab some candy from my box!"
Ezra looked nervous. "Uh . . ."
"Quick!" Glen said.
Ivy was already stuffing her pockets.
So was Glen. Ezra took a few pieces.
"Thanks, Mrs. Matsak!" Glen said.
As they left the office, even Ezra was giggling.
That night, after evening assembly, the kids walked to the cabins.
Ivy scratched her arm.
"Ugh! More mosquito bites. I hate this stupid camp!"
Ezra frowned. "You know where there aren't any mosquitos? The beach!"
"Cheer up," Glen said. "I'll give you more candy.
I promised to give some to Buck, Huck, and Chuck too.
They're coming to our cabin for it."
"You're giving candy to the Ucks? Why?" Ivy asked.
"You should keep it for us."
"Yeah, the Ucks are kind of mean," Ezra said.
Glen smiled. "Giving away candy will make me the most popular guy at camp!"
They got to the boys' cabin.
"Whoa!" Glen cried.
Ivy gasped. The door screen was torn open!
Glen slowly opened the door.
Inside, empty candy wrappers littered the floor!
The three friends stared at all the candy wrappers.
"What happened?" Glen asked.
"It must have been a wild animal."
Ezra pointed to the torn screen.
"I guess the rule about no food in the cabins is a good one."
"I wonder what kind of animal ate the candy," Ivy said.
Just then the Ucks walked in.
"Hey, kid," Huck said to Glen. "Where's our candy?"
Glen picked up the empty wrappers.
"Uh . . . I'm out of candy right now, but I'll get more tomorrow!"
He smiled and gave the Ucks a thumbs-up.
"They ate it all!" Chuck yelled.
"We didn't eat it," Ezra said.
"A wild animal broke in and stole it."
He tried to fix the torn screen.
A sly grin spread across Ivy's face.
"It was a bear. A huge, brown one!"
The Ucks stared at her and started laughing.
"Yeah, right," Buck said.
"Didn't you see it?" Ivy asked.
"It ran out of the cabin and into the woods."
Buck pointed at Glen.
"You'd better have candy for us tomorrow. Or else!"
"A bear!" Huck said.
"Who would believe a story like that?"
The Ucks walked away, still laughing.
Ivy ran to the door.
"You'll make good bear food!" she yelled.
"Bears always eat the dumb kids first!"
The next morning after breakfast, the three friends left the mess hall.
"I need to sneak into the office somehow," Glen said.
"I have to get candy for the Ucks."
He gulped, remembering Buck's threat. "Or else!"
"I'll help you, but don't let those bullies push you around," Ivy said.
Ezra was quiet.
"What's wrong?" Ivy asked.
"I miss my parents," Ezra said.
"I really wish I was at the beach with them." He sighed.
Ivy's eyes lit up.
"Let's go to the office.
You can call your parents, and we'll sneak Glen's candy out somehow."
Ezra smiled, and the three headed to the office.
"Attention, campers!" Mrs. Matsak's voice came over the PA system.
"Tomorrow Camp Evergreen's owner, Mr. Offal, will visit.
He has a special gift for us.
Everyone will meet in the square for the big ceremony."
"I bet the gift is the bear statue we saw yesterday." Glen shook his head.
"Ivy, why did you tell the Ucks that crazy bear story?"
Ivy laughed. "I was just having fun, trying to scare them."
They reached the office as Mrs. Matsak stepped outside.
"Mrs. Matsak?" Ezra cleared his throat.
"Could I please call my parents?"
"You've called them four times since camp started!" Mrs. Matsak said.
"But my last call was two weeks ago," Ezra said.
Mrs. Matsak sighed. "Fine. Keep it short."
Private walked up and saluted Mrs. Matsak.
"Ready for inspection?" Private asked.
Every morning the two women checked the campers' cabins to make sure they were clean.
As they walked away, Glen and Ivy fist-bumped each other.
"Perfect, we'll have the office to ourselves!" Glen said.
The kids went inside. Ezra went to make his phone call.
Glen and Ivy opened the cabinet where the packages were kept.
Glen took down his box, grabbed two brownies, and stuffed them in his mouth.
Ivy grabbed one too. Then they filled their pockets with candy.
Suddenly Ezra's voice boomed through the loudspeaker.
"But Mommy and Daddy! I miss you so much!
Don't you miss your Snuggy Wuggy?"
Glen and Ivy stared at each other.
Somehow Ezra's phone call could be heard through the PA system!
"Oh no!" Ivy thought as she and Glen ran to Ezra.
By accident, he'd switched on the PA system with his elbow.
Glen reached over and turned off the switch.
Ezra quickly said good-bye to his parents and ended his call.
He looked panicked. "Did everyone in camp just hear my phone call?"
"Um, only part of it," Ivy said.
"Yeah, only part of it." Glen patted him on the back. "The worst part."
"Ugh!" Ezra groaned.
Glen grabbed some more brownies and put the box away.
"Here, Ezra, have a brownie. Actually—have four brownies."
Ezra tried to eat one, but he was too worried. "I feel sick."
So Glen ate the brownies for him.
The kids left the office.
Outside, the Ucks were waiting along with Clara and Willow.
"Hey, Snuggy Wuggy!" Chuck yelled.
The Ucks roared with laughter.
"Do you miss your mommy and daddy, Snuggy Wuggy?" Huck asked.
Clara frowned at the three boys.
"I think it's sweet that Ezra misses his parents."
"Me too!" Willow said.
That just made the Ucks laugh harder.
Ivy looked at Ezra and saw that his face was bright red.
"Cut it out," she said to the Ucks.
"Hey, where's our candy?" Huck asked, holding out his hand.
Ivy crossed her arms. "You're not getting any candy from us!"
"Ha-ha! Ivy's kidding," Glen said.
"See, here's your candy."
